decision.explanation: For f(x)=arctan(x), f(1)=π/4, f'(x)=1/(1+x²), and f''(x)=-2x/(1+x²)². Thus f'(1)=1/2 and f''(1)=-1/2. The Taylor terms are f(1)+f'(1)(x-1)+f''(1)(x-1)²/2=π/4+(x-1)/2-(x-1)²/4, matching c.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Find the first three non-zero terms in the Taylor expansion of $\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x)$ about the point $x=1.$
after.worked_solution:
We use Taylor's theorem in the form

$$
f(x)=f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a)+\frac{{f}^{″}(a)}{2!}(x-a)^{2}+\frac{{f}^{‴}(a)}{3!}(x-a)^{3}+⋯,
$$

with $f(x)=\operatorname{arctan}⁡x$ and $a=1.$ 

Computing the required derivatives, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡x \\ f(1) & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡1=\frac{\pi }{4} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}} \\ {f}^{′}(1) & =\frac{1}{1+1}=\frac{1}{2} \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =-\frac{2x}{(1+{x}^{2})^{2}} \\ {f}^{″}(1) & =-\frac{2(1)}{(1+1)^{2}}=-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{arctan}⁡x & =\frac{\pi }{4}+(\frac{1}{2})(x-1)+\frac{1}{2!}(-\frac{1}{2})(x-1)^{2}+⋯ \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{1}{2}(x-1)-\frac{1}{4}(x-1)^{2}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: Find the first three non-zero terms in the Taylor expansion of $\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x)$ about the point $x=1.$
content.worked_solution:
We use Taylor's theorem in the form

$$
f(x)=f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a)+\frac{{f}^{″}(a)}{2!}(x-a)^{2}+\frac{{f}^{‴}(a)}{3!}(x-a)^{3}+⋯,
$$

with $f(x)=\operatorname{arctan}⁡x$ and $a=1.$ 

Computing the required derivatives, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡x \\ f(1) & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡1=\frac{\pi }{4} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}} \\ {f}^{′}(1) & =\frac{1}{1+1}=\frac{1}{2} \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =-\frac{2x}{(1+{x}^{2})^{2}} \\ {f}^{″}(1) & =-\frac{2(1)}{(1+1)^{2}}=-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{arctan}⁡x & =\frac{\pi }{4}+(\frac{1}{2})(x-1)+\frac{1}{2!}(-\frac{1}{2})(x-1)^{2}+⋯ \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{1}{2}(x-1)-\frac{1}{4}(x-1)^{2}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
